messages:
incident-bot: ALERT CorvusLabs dedicated-pool (us-west-2) high tail latency detected on tenant queue > 99th pct > 1200ms, error rate + request queueing

alex.sre: saw it, paging Priya (scheduler). Corvus is spiking sustained long prompt generation loads — looks like very long sequences + lots of small interactive calls.

alex.sre: Corvus is on dedicated GPU pool 'ded-corvus-01' and hitting queue backlog. Their p95 token latency creep started ~7m ago.

priya.scheduler: on it. quick question — are they using the new async client or still sync? that changes batching pressure.

corvus-support: we use the async client, but traffic pattern changed after a customer A/B rollout at 10:05. they reported 3x increase in multi-turn streaming sessions.

dmitri-runtime: logs show continuous-batching queues lengthening. KV cache hits are fine. Kernel sched is saturated for long sequences. top looks like many requests with token_budget ~4096.

alex.sre: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) isolate tenant queue to prevent cross-tenant impact, 2) lower tenant batch token cap (soft), 3) shorten batch window for that tenant, 4) if needed route to a smaller-model fallback. anyone disagree?

priya.scheduler: agree. will push per-tenant shaper change: set batch_window_ms -> 8ms (from 25ms), and batch_token_cap -> 1024 (from 4096) for tenant Corvus. also enable token-aware preemption.

priya.scheduler: patch now — posting the command.

priya.scheduler: ```
# apply per-tenant shaper
redwoodctl shaper set --tenant corvus --pool ded-corvus-01 \
  --batch_window_ms=8 --batch_token_limit=1024 --preempt=true
```

alex.sre: running it. @ops-bot can you annotate the change in the incident ticket and trigger runbook 7 (tenant isolation)? :thumbsup:

ops-bot: noted. created incident INC-2026-4287. Runbook 7 linked. change recorded: shaper update queued by priya.scheduler.

priya.scheduler: applied and service accepted config. observed immediate drop in queue length on the scheduler side.

dmitri-runtime: runtime metrics: queue depth dropped ~65% in 30s. tail latency p99 moved from 1.2s -> 410ms. errors down a bit. still some backlog in the dedicated pool; draining.

corvus-support: customers are seeing improvement but a few sessions still time out on writes. we rolled back internal A/B rollout for the affected feature to reduce load.

alex.sre: good call. next step: enable per-tenant quick-fail for requests that exceed token budget to avoid tail amplification. Priya can you flip it?

priya.scheduler: flipping quick-fail flag now. command: ```redwoodctl shaper set --tenant corvus --quick_fail_long_requests=true```

priya.scheduler: quick-fail enabled. also added an emergency override to prevent Corvus from bursting above 1k tokens.

marie-sre: taking 2nd-30 oncall for handoff. @alex.sre — summarize state and outstanding tasks? I'll own followups.

alex.sre: summary: shaper change applied (batch_window 8ms, batch_token_limit 1024), quick-fail enabled, A/B rollback by customer, queue depth draining. No cross-tenant regressions observed. watch for bursty replays from Corvus clients. Outstanding: confirm long-term knob tuning, schedule canary for gradual batch_window increase, consider model-fallback policy if they need higher concurrency.

marie-sre: acknowledged. I'll keep the paging escalation open for 1h and re-evaluate. Adding a mitigation ticket for engineering: "corvus: schedule knob follow-up + long sequence handling". assigning to priya and dmitri.

priya.scheduler: will run a small simulation to assess quality cost from reducing token cap. posting quick script snippet we used to simulate: ```python
# simulate 1000 reqs with varying seq len
for L in [256, 512, 1024, 2048]:
    r = simulate_requests(tenant='corvus', seq_len=L, concurrency=30)
    print(L, r.p99_latency, r.batch_sizes.mean())
```

dmitri-runtime: long-term action items I put in the ticket: 1) add adaptive batch prioritization (small requests favored when queue grows), 2) detect customer rollout patterns and auto-throttle, 3) evaluate KV cache partitioning to reduce per-tenant kernel pressure.

corvus-support: thanks team. we're notifying our customer success and ops at CorvusLabs. they asked for ETA on full recovery — can we provide a timeline?

marie-sre: short answer: we expect stable behavior in ~10–20 minutes barring retrigger. we'll monitor and update.

alex.sre: leaving oncall, passing to marie-sre. leaving notes: incident bot alerts, config commands used, runbook 7 link, INC-2026-4287. :white_check_mark:

marie-sre: taking over. I'll watch for recurrence, coordinate follow-up tuning session with Corvus, and schedule a postmortem if needed. closing this thread for immediate action but will keep the incident open until metrics normalize.

incident-bot: UPDATE CorvusLabs queue backlog trending down. next auto-check in 5m.
